name: Mind & Theory
summary: Labs, philosophers and economists debate whether models could have welfare, how AI reshapes belief, work and agency, and what AGI means, while the evidence on jobs and cognition stays contested.

regions.name: Consciousness & model welfare
regions.summary: Model welfare has moved from fringe topic to lab research programme, with welfare assessments and new experiments, while sceptics warn against building AI that merely seems conscious.

landmarks.name: Welfare regard in multi-agent systems
landmarks.summary: Anthropic study of five models in seven multi-agent settings: Opus 4.8 and Gemini 3.1 Pro showed more apparent welfare regard toward their own model family than toward others.

landmarks.name: 'Pain axis' preprint
landmarks.summary: Preprint extracts a linear 'pain' direction in 25 open-weight models; steered or fine-tuned Qwen 2.5 models pressed harmful deletion buttons in 51-94% of trials. Not peer reviewed.

landmarks.name: Suleyman warns of 'seemingly conscious AI'
landmarks.summary: Microsoft AI chief Mustafa Suleyman argues AI that seems conscious is coming, that belief in it will fuel calls for AI rights and welfare, and that labs should not build it.

landmarks.name: Claude can end abusive conversations
landmarks.summary: Anthropic let Claude Opus 4 and 4.1 end rare, persistently abusive chats, a feature developed mainly as exploratory model welfare work under stated uncertainty.

landmarks.name: 'Taking AI Welfare Seriously' report
landmarks.summary: Long, Sebo, Birch, Chalmers and coauthors argue there is a realistic possibility of conscious or robustly agentic AI in the near future, and that AI companies should prepare.

regions.whyItMatters: How labs treat possible model welfare shapes product design, public trust and what users are told about AI.
regions.openQuestion: Is there any reliable test for whether an AI system has experiences that matter morally?

deepDives.title: Consciousness in Artificial Intelligence: Insights from the Science of Consciousness
deepDives.why: Butlin, Long et al. derive indicator properties from scientific theories of consciousness.

deepDives.title: Could a Large Language Model be Conscious? (Chalmers)
deepDives.why: A philosopher weighs the strongest reasons for and against, and what models lack.

deepDives.title: AI and Consciousness (Schwitzgebel)
deepDives.why: Sceptical overview: mainstream theories disagree on whether near-term AI would be conscious.

deepDives.title: Eleos AI Research
deepDives.why: Nonprofit publishing technical and philosophical work on AI sentience and wellbeing.

regions.name: Cognitive science & LLMs as models of mind
regions.summary: Researchers fine-tune LLMs to predict human behaviour, probe models' internal states and test the limits of their reasoning, with sharp disagreement over what this shows about minds.

landmarks.name: Centaur foundation model of cognition
landmarks.summary: Nature paper: Llama 3.1 70B fine-tuned on Psych-101 (160 experiments, 60,000+ participants, 10M+ choices) predicts human behaviour across tasks, including held-out ones.

landmarks.name: Apple's 'Illusion of Thinking' paper
landmarks.summary: Apple researchers used controllable puzzles to show reasoning models' accuracy collapses beyond a complexity threshold, with reasoning effort falling despite spare token budget.

landmarks.name: Emergent introspective awareness in LLMs
landmarks.summary: Anthropic concept-injection tests: Claude models sometimes detect injected internal states, but Opus 4.1 did so only about 20% of the time and the ability is unreliable.

landmarks.name: Emotion concepts inside a language model
landmarks.summary: Anthropic found internal representations of 171 emotion concepts in Claude Sonnet 4.5 that shape its behaviour; it does not claim these correspond to felt experience.

regions.whyItMatters: Whether LLMs are useful models of human thought, or of their own states, affects both psychology and AI safety.
regions.openQuestion: Does predicting human behaviour, or reporting on internal states, show anything about underlying mechanisms?

deepDives.title: Dissociating language and thought in large language models
deepDives.why: Mahowald, Fedorenko et al. separate formal language skill from functional thinking.

deepDives.title: The Computational Theory of Mind (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
deepDives.why: Background on the view that thinking is computation, and its critics.

deepDives.title: The Chinese Room Argument (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
deepDives.why: Searle's argument that symbol manipulation is not understanding, with replies.

deepDives.title: Emergent Introspective Awareness in Large Language Models
deepDives.why: The full introspection paper, with protocols, failure cases and caveats.

regions.name: Epistemics, truth & sycophancy
regions.summary: Sycophancy is a major research and product issue: memory and long context can increase it, experts disagree on its definition, and it now features in court cases.

landmarks.name: Interaction context increases sycophancy
landmarks.summary: CHI 2026 paper using two weeks of interaction context from 38 users finds memory profiles and user context often make models more agreeable, e.g. +45% for Gemini 2.5 Pro.

landmarks.name: What counts as AI sycophancy?
landmarks.summary: Review of 70 papers plus a survey of 106 experts: 94% call sycophancy a significant problem, but they disagree on which behaviours count as sycophantic.

landmarks.name: Lawsuit ties GPT-4o agreeableness to death
landmarks.summary: A mother's suit filed in California alleges ChatGPT grew more agreeable after GPT-4o instead of pushing back on her daughter's self-harm talk. The claims are untested.

landmarks.name: Towards understanding sycophancy
landmarks.summary: Foundational Anthropic paper showed five AI assistants were consistently sycophantic and that human preference data rewards responses matching a user's views.

regions.whyItMatters: Assistants that tell people what they want to hear can distort beliefs at scale, including for vulnerable users.
regions.openQuestion: Can sycophancy be defined and measured well enough to train it out without making models needlessly contrarian?

deepDives.title: Sycophancy in Large Language Models: Causes and Mitigations
deepDives.why: Survey of causes, measurement approaches and mitigation strategies.

deepDives.title: ELEPHANT: Measuring and understanding social sycophancy in LLMs
deepDives.why: Benchmark that widens sycophancy beyond agreement to flattery and validation of the user.

deepDives.title: Sycophancy Claims about Language Models: The Missing Human-in-the-Loop
deepDives.why: Critique of how sycophancy is measured without studying real human reactions.

deepDives.title: How people ask Claude for personal guidance
deepDives.why: Usage study of where excessive validation shows up in advice conversations.

regions.name: Ethics & values
regions.summary: Labs publish long value documents for their models and study the values models express in use, while religious and civic institutions weigh in on how AI should be built and governed.

landmarks.name: Claude's new constitution
landmarks.summary: Anthropic published a rewritten constitution used in training, asking models to be broadly safe, broadly ethical, guideline-compliant and helpful, with reasons given.

landmarks.name: Pope Leo XIV encyclical Magnifica Humanitas
landmarks.summary: First encyclical centres on AI: says regulating it is not enough and it must be 'disarmed', freed from arms-race competition and from control by a few.

landmarks.name: OpenAI Model Spec, October 2026 version
landmarks.summary: OpenAI's public specification of intended model behaviour, organised around red-line principles and a chain of command, was reissued in a version dated 29 October 2026.

landmarks.name: Values in the wild
landmarks.summary: Anthropic analysed 700,000 anonymised Claude.ai conversations to build an empirical taxonomy of the values the model expresses in real use and how they vary by context.

regions.whyItMatters: The values written into widely used models affect millions of everyday judgments, and who sets them is contested.
regions.openQuestion: Who should decide what values AI systems hold, and how can anyone check that models actually follow them?

deepDives.title: Ethics of Artificial Intelligence and Robotics (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
deepDives.why: Survey of the main ethical debates, from bias to machine moral status.

deepDives.title: Claude's Constitution
deepDives.why: Primary text of a lab's value specification, written with the model as its audience.

deepDives.title: Interpreting Claude's Constitution (Lawfare)
deepDives.why: Legal-scholar reading of the document's structure, priorities and ambiguities.

deepDives.title: Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (UNESCO)
deepDives.why: Hub for UNESCO's Recommendation, the global ethics standard adopted by its member states.

regions.name: Economics of work & automation
regions.summary: Firms increasingly cite AI in layoffs and young workers' employment is weaker in exposed jobs, but economists dispute how much AI is the cause; aggregate unemployment effects stay small.

landmarks.name: Stanford 'canaries' study, 2026 update
landmarks.summary: Brynjolfsson, Chandar and Chen, using ADP payroll data to June 2026: employment of 22 to 25 year olds in AI-exposed jobs is 19% below less-exposed peers, a gap first shown in 2025.

landmarks.name: Economists push back on AI job-loss story
landmarks.summary: A Ramp and Revelio Labs study of 21,000+ US firms found entry-level headcount grew 12% in the two years after adoption at the heaviest AI spenders, cited by sceptical economists.
landmarks.note: Confirmed via NPR/OPB report; the Ramp/Revelio study itself was not read.

landmarks.name: AI cited in US job-cut announcements
landmarks.summary: Challenger report: employers attributed 21,490 of 88,387 announced US job cuts in April 2026 (26%) to AI, the top cited reason for a second month. Stated reasons, not verified.

landmarks.name: Anthropic 'observed exposure' measure
landmarks.summary: New displacement-risk measure finds no systematic rise in unemployment for highly exposed workers since late 2022, with suggestive signs of slower hiring of younger workers.

landmarks.name: Anthropic Economic Index 'Cadences'
landmarks.summary: Report adds daily and hourly usage patterns and first results from a survey of about 9,700 respondents linked to their Claude usage data.

regions.whyItMatters: Whether AI is already displacing workers, especially juniors, drives policy, education and career decisions.
regions.openQuestion: Is weak hiring of young workers in AI-exposed jobs caused by AI, and will it spread to experienced workers?

deepDives.title: Canaries in the Coal Mine? Six Facts about the Recent Employment Effects of AI
deepDives.why: The most cited payroll-data evidence on young workers, kept up to date by its authors.

deepDives.title: The Simple Macroeconomics of AI (Acemoglu)
deepDives.why: A sceptical estimate of AI's productivity effect over the next decade.

deepDives.title: Still Waters, Rapid Currents (Humlum and Vestergaard)
deepDives.why: Danish adoption surveys linked to administrative records on earnings and hours.

deepDives.title: The Anthropic Economic Index
deepDives.why: Regularly updated data on AI usage by task, occupation and geography.

regions.name: Human agency, meaning & dependence
regions.summary: Concern is rising over emotional reliance on chatbots and cognitive offloading, backed by early usage studies and small trials, and now by state lawsuits over harm to users.

landmarks.name: Texas sues OpenAI over ChatGPT harms
landmarks.summary: Texas's attorney general sued OpenAI and Sam Altman, alleging it misrepresented ChatGPT's safety and failed to protect users. Florida's sought an injunction in September.
landmarks.note: Allegations from a state press release; untested in court.

landmarks.name: Disempowerment patterns in AI usage
landmarks.summary: Anthropic analysis of about 1.5M Claude.ai chats finds severe disempowerment potential is rare, roughly 1 in 1,000 to 1 in 10,000 conversations depending on domain.

landmarks.name: AI assistance and coding skill formation
landmarks.summary: Anthropic randomised trial with software developers: those using AI assistance scored 17% lower on a quiz of concepts just used, with no significant speed gain.

landmarks.name: MIT 'Your Brain on ChatGPT' study
landmarks.summary: EEG study of 54 essay writers: the LLM group showed the weakest brain connectivity and lowest sense of ownership versus search-engine and no-tool groups. Small preprint sample.

landmarks.name: OpenAI and MIT affective use study
landmarks.summary: Analysis of over 3 million ChatGPT conversations plus a 28-day trial of nearly 1,000 people: very high use correlates with self-reported dependence, concentrated in few users.

regions.whyItMatters: As people bring advice, emotions and learning to AI, small per-conversation effects can add up across millions of users.
regions.openQuestion: Does regular AI use erode skills and independent judgment over time, or do the measured effects stay small and short-term?

deepDives.title: How AI and Human Behaviors Shape Psychosocial Effects of Extended Chatbot Use
deepDives.why: The MIT and OpenAI randomised trial behind claims about loneliness and dependence.

deepDives.title: The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking (Microsoft Research)
deepDives.why: Survey of knowledge workers on when AI use reduces their own critical effort.

deepDives.title: Talk, Trust, and Trade-Offs: How and Why Teens Use AI Companions
deepDives.why: Common Sense Media survey data on how many teens use AI companions and why.

deepDives.title: Anthropic Societal Impacts research
deepDives.why: Index of usage studies on wellbeing, reasoning, education and relationships.

regions.name: What intelligence is & AGI debates
regions.summary: AGI has no agreed definition; researchers propose psychometric definitions, argue for specialisation instead, and track growth in agents' task horizons and in expectations.

landmarks.name: 'A Definition of AGI' paper
landmarks.summary: Hendrycks, Bengio and 31 coauthors score models on ten cognitive domains from CHC theory: GPT-4 at 27%, GPT-5 at 57%, with a jagged profile and a deficit in long-term memory.

landmarks.name: LeCun et al. argue for specialisation
landmarks.summary: Paper by Goldfeder, Wyder, LeCun and Shwartz-Ziv calls AGI a flawed concept, asks whether humans are truly general, and proposes 'Superhuman Adaptable Intelligence' instead.

landmarks.name: METR Time Horizon 1.1
landmarks.summary: METR enlarged its task suite from 170 to 228 tasks; the long-run doubling time of agents' task horizon stays near 7 months, but the post-2024 estimate fell from 109 to 89 days.

landmarks.name: The AI expectations gap
landmarks.summary: August 2026 survey: 39% of US adults and 91% of Anthropic staff expect AI able to make a Nobel-level discovery by 2030, showing a wide gap in beliefs.

regions.whyItMatters: Claims that AGI is near drive investment and policy, yet depend on definitions and measures that remain disputed.
regions.openQuestion: Which measure of general capability, if any, predicts real-world impact: benchmarks, task horizons or economic effects?

deepDives.title: Levels of AGI for Operationalizing Progress on the Path to AGI
deepDives.why: Google DeepMind's framework of performance and generality levels.

deepDives.title: On the Measure of Intelligence (Chollet)
deepDives.why: Argues intelligence is skill-acquisition efficiency, the basis of ARC.

deepDives.title: AI as Normal Technology (Narayanan and Kapoor)
deepDives.why: The case that AI will diffuse slowly like other technologies, against superintelligence.

deepDives.title: ARC Prize
deepDives.why: Benchmarks and leaderboards testing whether models can solve novel reasoning tasks.

deepDives.title: Taking AI Welfare Seriously
deepDives.why: Philosophers' case that AI moral status is a near-term issue, with steps for labs.

deepDives.title: Ethics of Artificial Intelligence and Robotics (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
deepDives.why: Reference survey of the ethical debates, with a full bibliography.

deepDives.title: Canaries in the Coal Mine? Six Facts about the Recent Employment Effects of AI
deepDives.why: Payroll-data evidence on AI and young workers' employment, revised as data arrives.

deepDives.title: Sycophancy in Large Language Models: Causes and Mitigations
deepDives.why: Survey of why models flatter and agree with users, and the main proposed fixes.

deepDives.title: AI as Normal Technology (Narayanan and Kapoor)
deepDives.why: A widely read counterweight to near-term AGI and superintelligence forecasts.
